text:
emily: Quick UX question — prototype up at https://redwood.design/prototypes/form-errors-compact I split two approaches in the prototype: 1) inline field-level errors (icon + red helper text) that appear on blur, and 2) a small persistent top banner that summarizes errors with jump links to fields. Which approach should be default for the console forms? Also debating required indicators (asterisk vs explicit 'Required' label) and destructive confirmations (typed confirm vs modal+undo). Thoughts? chris: I lean inline for field-specific issues — it's immediate and helps people fix in context. Banner makes sense for submission/server-side failures or when multiple fields are invalid at once. Important a11y bits: inline error nodes need role="alert" and focus management to move focus to the first invalid field after submit. chris: Example snippet we should standardize in the component lib: ```
Please enter a valid email
``` matt: Agree with inline-first. A couple notes on required markers: do NOT rely on color alone. The asterisk is ok visually but we must expose it to screen readers (visually-hidden text like Required) or use `aria-required` on the control. Also our current asterisk color fails contrast at 12px — accessibility check needed. rachel: For destructive actions — typed-confirm (e.g., type org name) is good for very high-blast actions (delete org, purge data). It's heavy for daily actions. Prefer modal confirm + undo for most deletes. If we keep typed-confirm, make copy explicit: what will be deleted, any downstream impact, and exact text to type. Example microcopy: "This will permanently delete the org and all associated models. Type the full org name to confirm." emily: Good call on contrast — I noticed the asterisk uses token `text-muted` which is too low. Maybe bold it or move to `text-primary` for form labels. Also on mobile, inline errors can push content a lot; the compact top banner with jump links might be friendlier there. chris: +1 to a mobile-only banner fallback. Also, we should standardize keyboard focus flow: after a submit with errors, focus should land on the first invalid field, and the banner (if present) should have an accessible summary like "Form contains 3 errors" with links that move focus. matt: Minor nit — avoid vague prompts like "Are you sure?". Use consequence-first copy: "Deleting this workspace will remove X users and Y projects immediately. This action cannot be undone." :warning: rachel: Product asks for telemetry: can we add an event when typed-confirm modal is used vs regular modal so we can measure friction? If typed-confirm prevents mistakes but reduces conversions maybe we need thresholds. design-bot: FYI — design token update in v3.2: danger color is now `#d9534f`. Update components that hardcode the old value. chris: I'll put together a small PR to the component library with: (a) `FormError` pattern examples (inline + banner) and aria examples, (b) a11y tests for contrast and focus, and (c) mobile banner fallback. matt: I'll run the contrast audit and list any labels/asterisks that fail. rachel: I'll draft a decision doc for when typed-confirm is allowed (criteria: irreversible data loss, legal/regulatory impact, >10 teams/orgs affected). emily: Thanks everyone. Action items recap: Chris -> component PR and aria snippets; Matt -> accessibility audit on asterisks/labels; Rachel -> typed-confirm decision doc + telemetry ask; Emily -> update prototype copy and mobile banner variant. Back with updates by EOW? :thumbsup: chris: :thumbsup: matt: :+1: rachel: Sounds good
